title: Plastic Bottle

actions.label: Rinse & Empty Bottle
actions.feedback: Bottle rinsed and emptied. Eliminates liquid residue that contaminates paper bales and sorting equipment.

actions.label: Remove Bottle Cap
actions.feedback: Cap separated. Note: Rules differ by area—some facilities ask you to keep caps screwed on tightly so they do not fall through sorting screens, while others ask for separate collection.

outcomes.title: Plastic Recycling Accepted
outcomes.text: Clean, empty PET bottles are accepted in the Blue Recycling Bin for high-grade bottle-to-bottle reprocessing.
outcomes.takeaway: Always rinse and empty beverage containers before recycling.

outcomes.title: Recycling Stream Contaminated
outcomes.text: Residual liquids spill onto dry paper and cardboard in collection trucks, ruining recyclable paper fibers and attracting pests at the MRF.
outcomes.takeaway: Unrinsed containers can cause entire truckloads of dry recyclables to be rejected.

outcomes.title: Recyclable Resource Landfilled
outcomes.text: PET plastic takes over 400 years to decompose in landfills, releasing microplastics and wasting valuable recyclable polymers.
outcomes.takeaway: Rinsing and placing in the Blue Recycling Bin saves energy and landfill space.

outcomes.title: Compost Contamination
outcomes.text: Petroleum-derived PET plastics do not biodegrade in compost and contaminate organic compost batches with non-degradable fragments.
outcomes.takeaway: Never place plastics in green organic compost bins.

guidanceNote: Consistent with app guidance: Rinse & place in Blue Recycling Bin. Cap action is informational and never penalized.
